title: The Hat-Trick (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational cricket philosophy 106bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal absurdist sport family
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The hat-trick is three wickets from three consecutive deliveries
A thing so rare it stops the whole ground and all its memories
The first one is a wicket — good bowling, move along
The second raises eyebrows and the crowd begins its song

[Pre-Chorus]
The third delivery carries everything the game has ever held
Every hat-trick ever bowled sits in that ball propelled

[Chorus]
The hat-trick is the rarest thing the cricket ground will see
Three balls, three wickets, a moment that will live in history
The hat-trick takes a lifetime and three seconds to complete
And no one who achieves it ever thinks the job is neat
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
The field goes tight around the bat for the hat-trick ball
Every position filled with someone ready for the call
The batsman knows, the fielders know, the umpire knows the weight
The hat-trick ball arrives with all of cricket's entire fate

[Bridge]
Mine was in the garden with my brother on the lawn
A rubber ball, a garbage bin, a Tuesday early morn
I got him three times running and he said the last one didn't count
I disagreed and that disagreement continues to this amount

[Outro]
Hat-trick knows… three in a row changes the whole room… hat-trick knows
That's my boy
